questions.q: Identify the pair of elements in which the difference in atomic radii is maximum
questions.solution:
1- C and N both element are in same period carbon has atomic radius approximately 70 pm . While nitrogen has 65 pm . So the difference is $(70-65)=5 \mathrm{pm}$ )
2- O and F are in the same period oxygen atomic radius is 60 pm . Fluorine has atomic radius approximately 50 pm . So the difference $-(60-50)=10 \mathrm{pm}$.
3- $\mathbf{P}$ has atomic radius of approximately 100 pm . While sulfur has atomic radius 100 pm . So there will be no difference.
4- Li has atomic radius of approximately 155 pm while Be has atomic Radius of 105 pm . So the difference is $(155-105)=50 \mathrm{pm} . \mathrm{Li}$ and Be have the maximum difference.

questions.solution:

Among oxygen and sulphur, sulphur has a higher electron gain enthalpy than oxygen due to larger size and greater effective nuclear charge.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Choose the correct order of second ionisation enthalpies Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen and Fluorine.
questions.solution:
The corresponding electronic configurations for the given species are:
$\mathrm{C}: 1 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{p}^2, \mathrm{~N}: 1 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{p}^3, \mathrm{O}: 1 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{p}^4$
F : $1 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{~s}^2 2 \mathrm{p}^5$.
Since there are three 2 p-orbitals in the 2 p-subshell, it is evident that the loss of a second electron from the valence shell will be most difficult in oxygen as it would disturb the stable half-filled p-subshell.
The removal of second electron will be easiest for carbon as it would give a fully-filled $2 \mathrm{~s}$-subshell.
Thus, the order of second ionization energy will be:Oxygen > Fluorine > Nitrogen > Carbon

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The correct order of decreasing acidic nature of oxides
questions.solution:
A binary compound of oxygen with another element is called oxide

Oxides can be simple (e.g., MgO, Al2O3 ) or mixed (Pb3O4 ,Fe3O4 ). Simple oxides can be classified on the basis of their acidic, basic or amphoteric character. An oxide that combines with water to give an acid is termed acidic oxide (e.g., SO2 ,Cl2O7,CO2 , N2O5 ). For example, SO2 combines with water to give H2SO3 , an acid.

 The oxides which give a base with water are known as basic oxides (e.g., Na2O, CaO, BaO). For example, CaO combines with water to give Ca(OH)2, a base.

Some metallic oxides exhibit a dual behaviour. They show characteristics of both acidic as well as basic oxides. Such oxides are known as amphoteric oxides. They react with acids as well as alkalies. For example, Al2O3 reacts with acids as well as alkalies.

There are some oxides which are neither acidic nor basic. Such oxides are known as neutral oxides. Examples of neutral oxides are CO, NO and N2O.

  Group 1 Group 2 Group 13 Group 14 Group 15
Period 2 Li Be B C N

According to periodic trend, the electronegativity of the period 2 elements increases in the order :

Li < Be < B < C < N

Electronegativty of the  central atom of the oxide is direclty proportional acidic nature of the oxide.

Therefore, the acidic character of their oxides decreases in the order as follows :

N2O3 > CO2 > B2O3 > BeO > Li2O

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?

(a) 'He' is the second most abundant element in the universe.

(b) the symbol for the element with atomic number 110 is Ds.

(c) Osmium has the highest density among all elements.

(d) Francium is the most electropositive element in the periodic table.
questions.solution:
(a) 'He' is the second most abundant element in the universe. The most abundant element in the universe is hydrogen, which makes up about three-quarters of all matter, Helium makes up most of the remaining 25%.

(b) Darmstadtium is a chemical element with the symbol Ds and atomic number 110. It is an extremely radioactive synthetic element.

(c) Under ordinary conditions of temperature and pressure, osmium is the element with the highest density. Its density is 22.59 g/cm3.

(d) Francium is the most electropositive element in the periodic table.

So, all these statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The electronegativity order of the following elements is
questions.solution: Electronegativity is inversely proportional to the atomic size. Smaller the size, greater is the electronegativity. Nitrogen is placed in second period, so it has smallest size and highest electronegativity. Then, iodine belongs to halogen family which are electronegative elements. For, S and Te, on moving top to bottom, atomic size increases so electronegative character decreases. So, the correct order is $\mathrm{N}\gt \mathrm{I}\gt \mathrm{S}\gt \mathrm{Te}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following is not a periodic property?
questions.solution:
Apart from radioactivity, all are periodic properties.

Radioactivity is a process in which nuclei of certain elements undergo spontaneous disintegration and it does not depend on configuration, so it is not periodic property. Atomic size, electron affinity and ionisation potential are the property which vary or which show regular trend according to the electronic configuration of elements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The correct increasing order of the electronegativity is
questions.solution:
According to the question, Electronegativity is a chemical property that describes the power of an atom in a molecule to attract electrons to itself. There is a large difference in electronegativity for atoms from the left- and right-hand sides of the periodic table.

The value of electronegativity of chlorine atom is 3.0, the electronegativity of sulphur atom is 2.5, The electronegativity of carbon atom is 2.5 (affected by other factors), the value of electronegativity is of boron is 2.0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the given atoms has the greatest electron affinity?
questions.solution:
According to the question, Electron affinity is the amount of energy required to detach one electron from a negatively charged ion of an atom or molecule. It is indicated using the symbol Ea and is usually expressed in units of kJ/mol. Electron affinity follows a trend on the periodic table. It is an exothermic process. 

Fluorine has lower electron affinity than chlorine because of the small size of fluorine which results in stronger repulsion between the electron and the electrons already present in the atom of fluorine. Hence, the energy released in accepting an electron is lesser in fluorine than that of chlorine.

Electron affinity of fluorine is -333 kJ/mol-1And The value of electron affinity of chlorine is -349 kJ/mol-1

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The basic difference in approach between Mendeleev's periodic law and modern periodic law is the change on the basis of classification of elements from
questions.solution:
The basic difference in approach between Mendeleev's periodic law and Modern periodic. law is as follows :
The Mendeleev's periodic law is based on atomic weight while modern periodic law is based on atomic number. i.e. according to Mendeleev's periodic law.
If the element are arranged in order of increasing atomic weights their properties vary in definite manner from member to member of the series, but return more or less nearly to same value at certain fixed points in the series, while according to modern periodic law.
Physical and chemical properties of the elements are periodic function of their atomic numbers.

questions.q:
The successive ionisation energy values for an element ' $X$ ' are given below :
(i) lst ionisation energy $=410 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
(ii) $2 \mathrm{nd}$ ionisation energy $=820 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
iii) $3 \mathrm{rd}$ ionisation energy $=1100 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
(iv) 4 th ionisation energy $=1500 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
(v) 5 th ionisation energy $=3200 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
questions.solution: Maximum difference is between the fifth and fourth ionisation energy. (Removal of the 5 th electron requires almost more than double the energy required to remove the 4th electron.) This implies that the first four electrons are removed from the valence shell. Hence, number of valence electrons in the atom ' $X$ ' will be four.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
Which one among the following statements is/are not correct?
I. Ba compounds, generally are more covalent than Be compounds.
II. The electron gain enthalpy of $\mathrm{He}$ is positive.
III. The oxidation state of $\mathrm{O}$ in $\mathrm{OF}_2$ and $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{O}$ are same.
IV. The radius of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ion is smaller than that of $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ion.
questions.solution:
The explanation of given statements are:
I. Both beryllium ( $\mathrm{Be}$ ) and barium ( $\mathrm{Ba}$ ) belongs to the same group (i.e. group-II) and as we move down the group, size of atom/ion increases while their covalent character decreases. Thus, Ba compounds are generally less covalent than Be compounds.
Therefore, the given statement is not correct.
II. The electron gain enthalpy of $\mathrm{He}$ is positive because of very small size with full-filled electronic configuration. (i.e. $1 s^2$ ). Hence, the given statement is correct.
III. The oxidation state of $\mathrm{O}$ in $\mathrm{OF}_2=+1$ and oxidation state of $\mathrm{O}$ in $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{O}=-1$. Hence, the given statement is not correct.

IV. The radius of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ion is smaller than $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ion because both are isoelectronic species but $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ has less number of protons (i.e. more number of electrons) [i.e. $\mathrm{F}$ has 9 protons], than, that of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$(has 11 protons).
Hence, $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ion is of smaller in size than that of $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ion (due to greater attractive force in sodium.)
Thus, I and III are not the correct statements.
Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Among isoelectronic species, when negative charge present at atomic species than radii of species increase in comparison of parent atom. But there are two exceptions, in the case of Be and N because of the highly stable 2s2 (completely filled subshell) and 2s22p3 (half-filled subshell 2p3) valence configuration. B<Be<C<O<N.

As an additional electrons occupies the electrons in outer shell and protons in the nucleus. So, the $Z_{\text {eff }}$ increases.
As an neutral atoms that have Iost an $e^{-}$exhibit a positive charge and are called cations and therefore $Z_{\text {eff }}$ increases.

(i) Acidic property increases with the increase in oxidation number of the central atom (element) and for same oxidation number acidic nature increases along the period (according to long form periodic table). So, this statement is correct.

So, the ionic size order will be

M^{2-}>M^{-}>M^{+}>M^{2+} \text {. }

Thus, this statement is correct.
(iv) For 2nd I.E, the electron is removed from $M^{+}$ion.
$\because \mathrm{K}^{+}$has fully-filled noble gas configuration while $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$has full-filled $d^{10}$ configuration and $\mathrm{K}$ has no $d$-subshell. Thus, 2nd I.E for $\mathrm{K}^{+}$is more than of $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ion.
Hence, statement (iv) is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
Assertion (A) $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ are isoelectronic but the magnitude of ionic radius of $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ is less than that in $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$.
Reason $(R)$ The effective nuclear charge on the outermost electrons in $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ is greater than that in $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$.

The correct option among the following is
options: $A$ is true, $R$ is true and $R$ is the correct explanation for A.
$A$ is true, $R$ is true but $R$ is not the correct explanation for $A$.
questions.solution:
Higher the electrostatic attraction between nucleus and valence electron, smaller will be the size of the atom/ion.
Electrostatic attraction is given by $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}=Z-S$ where, $Z=$ the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom or ion (the atomic number) and $S=$ shielding from core electrons.
In case of $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$, they are isoelectronic species and thus have same number of electrons as $1 s^2, 2 s^2, 2 p^6$ isoelectric series of atoms and ions with different numbers of protons (and thus different nuclear attraction, gives) the relative ionic sizes of each atom or ion with respect to atomic number.
Atomic number, $Z_{\mathrm{Al}}=13$ and $Z_{\mathrm{Mg}}=12$.
Thus, $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ has lower ionic radii than $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$ due to higher nuclear charge.
Hence, A is true, $\mathrm{R}$ is true and $\mathrm{R}$ is the correct explanation for A.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In photoelectric effect, if the energy required to overcome the attractive forces on the electron, (work functions) of $\mathrm{Li}, \mathrm{Na}$ and $\mathrm{Rb}$ are $2.41 \mathrm{eV}$, $2.30 \mathrm{eV}$ and $2.09 \mathrm{eV}$ respectively, the work function of ' $\mathrm{K}$ ' could approximately be in $\mathrm{eV}$
questions.solution:
As the size of atom (element) increases, energy required to overcome the attractive force on outermost electron decreases.
$\mathrm{Li}, \mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{K}$ and $\mathrm{Rb}$ are the members of same group and have the following order of size
$\mathrm{Li} \lt  \mathrm{Na} \lt  \mathrm{K} \lt  \mathrm{Rb}$
Thus, the energy in case of $\mathrm{K}$ is intermediate of $\mathrm{Rb}$ and $\mathrm{Na}$, i.e.,
$2.30 \lt  \mathrm{K}\gt 2.09$
or the energy for $\mathrm{K}$ is $2.20 \mathrm{eV}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which one of the following is correct order of second ionisation potential of $\mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{Ne}, \mathrm{Mg}$ and $\mathrm{Al}$ ?
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{Ne}, \mathrm{Mg}$ and $\mathrm{Al}$ after the removal of an electron is as
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{Na}^{+}: 1 s^2, 2 s^2, 2 p^6 \\
& \mathrm{Ne}^{+}: 1 s^2, 2 s^2, 2 p^5 \\
& \mathrm{Mg}^{+}: 1 s^2, 2 s^2, 2 p^6, 3 s^1 \\
& \mathrm{Al}^{+}: 1 s^2, 2 s^2, 2 p^6, 3 s^2
\end{aligned}$
The ionisation energy decreases as the size of the atom/ion increases. Further ionisation energy increases with increase in nuclear charge.

Since, $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$gives a stable electronic configuration hence its $\mathrm{IE}_2$ is highest among the given species and therefore the correct order of their $\mathrm{IE}_2$ is
$\mathrm{Mg} \lt  \mathrm{Al} \lt  \mathrm{Ne} \lt  \mathrm{Na}$

questions.solution:
Elements having half or completely-filled orbitals, ie, having stable electronic configuration have very low negative value of electron affinity.
Since, the electron affinity of $B$ is lowest among the given, it has stable electronic configuration, $i e, 3 s^2, 3 p^3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which one of the following order is correct for the first ionisation energies of the elements?
questions.solution:
First ionisation energy increases in a period. Thus, the first IE of the elements of the second period should be as follows
$\mathrm{Be} \lt  \mathrm{B} \lt  \mathrm{N} \lt  \mathrm{O}$
But in practice, the elements do not follow the above order. The first IE of these elements is
$\mathrm{B} \lt  \mathrm{Be} \lt  \mathrm{O} \lt  \mathrm{N}$
The lower IE of $\mathrm{B}$ than that of $\mathrm{Be}$ is because in $\mathrm{B}\left(1 s^2, 2 s^2 2 p^1\right)$, electron is to be removed from $2 p$ which is easy while in $\operatorname{Be}\left(1 s^2, 2 s^2\right)$, electron is to be removed from $2 s$ which is difficult. The low IE of $\mathrm{O}$ than that of $\mathrm{N}$ is because of the half-filled $2 p$ orbitals in $\mathrm{N}\left(1 s^2, 2 s^2 2 p^3\right)$.

All transition elements are $d$-block elements but all $d$-block elements are not transition metals. A transition metal is one which forms one or more stable ions which have incomplete $d$-orbitals. questions.q:
The atomic numbers of elements $A, B, C$ and $D$ are $Z-1, Z, Z+1$ and $Z+2$, respectively. If ' $B$ ' is a noble gas, choose the correct answers from the following statements

questions.solution:
Given,
Atomic number of element $B=Z$
( $\because$ noble gas $\quad \therefore$ belong to zero group)
Atomic number of element $A=Z-1$
(ie, halogens)
Atomic number of element $C=Z+1$
(ie, group IA)
Atomic number of element $D=Z+2$
(ie, group IIA)
$\because$ Element $B$ is a noble gas
$\therefore$ Element $A$ must be a halogen ie, have highest electron affinity.
and element $C$ must be an alkali metal and exist in +1 oxidation state.
and element $D$ must be an alkaline earth metal with +2 oxidation state.

questions.q: The number of elements present in the fourth period is
questions.solution:
For 4th period, $n=4$.
Orbitals being filled $=4 s, 3 d, 4 p$
Number of elements in the period $=2,10,6=18$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following elements has the lowest melting point?
questions.solution:
The melting point order of IV A group elements is

\mathrm{C}>\mathrm{Si}>\text { Ge }>\mathrm{Pb}>\mathrm{Sn}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The electronic configuration of elements $A, B$ and $C$ are $[\mathrm{He}] 2 s^1,[\mathrm{Ne}] 3 s^1$ and [Ar] $4 s^1$ respectively, which one of the following order is correct for the first ionization potentials (in $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) of $A, B$ and $C$ ?
questions.solution:
Ionisation potential of $A, B$ and $C$ elements decreases with the ease of removal of electron from $A$ to $C$. Atomic size increase from $A$ to $C$, hence ionisation potential decrease in the same order.
So, order of ionisation potential is $A\gt B\gt C$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Ionic radius (in $Å$ ) of $\mathrm{As}^{3+}, \mathrm{Sb}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Bi}^{3+}$ follow the order
questions.solution: Ionic radius increases in a group from top to bottom i.e., it increases from $\mathrm{As}^{3+}$ to $\mathrm{Bi}^{3+}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following is the most basic oxide?
questions.solution: Dxygen is common in all oxides of group 16, and electronegativity decreases as we down the group thus basic nature of oxide increase. Herse PoO is the most basic oxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The element with atomic number 12 belongs to ......... group and ......... period
questions.solution:
Electronic configuration of $Z=12$ is
$1 s^2, 2 s^2, 2 p^4, 3 s^2$
Number of electrons in least orbit $=2$ i.e., group $=$ II A
Valence shell is 3 rd shell, so period $=3$ period
